title: The raise conversation
situation: You've been at the company a year. When your teammate Priya left, you took over her reporting work and still shipped the billing migration. Your pay hasn't changed. You booked 20 minutes with your manager.
goal: Ask for a specific raise and leave with a clear next step, not a "we'll see."

partner.name: Marcus Lee
partner.hiddenWant: To keep you. He has a small budget for exceptions, but he needs strong evidence to argue your case with HR.
digsInWhen: You use another offer as a threat

rubric.name: Backed it with impact
rubric.tip: Lead with one result he can repeat to someone else, with a number in it.

rubric.name: Named a clear ask
rubric.tip: Say the number out loud, early. A range invites the bottom of it.

rubric.name: Asked without apologising
rubric.tip: Drop "sorry" and "I know it's a bad time." Just say why you're here.

rubric.name: Left with a next step
rubric.description: Ended with a task and a date
rubric.tip: Before you leave, ask what he needs from you and by when.

partnerLine.guarded: Sure. I've got about ten minutes, actually. What's up?
partnerLine.neutral: Sure, I've got twenty minutes. What's up?
partnerLine.open: Hey, good timing. What's on your mind?

choices.text: I want to talk about my pay. This year I took on Priya's work and shipped the billing migration, and I think my salary should reflect that.
choices.reaction: Okay. That's fair to bring up. Walk me through it.
choices.coachNote: You named the topic and the reason in one breath, with no apology.

choices.text: So, um, this might be awkward, but is there any room to revisit my compensation at some point?
choices.reaction: At some point? Sure, I guess. What are you thinking?
choices.coachNote: Polite, but "might be awkward" and "at some point" tell him this can wait.
choices.betterLine: I'd like to talk about my pay. My role has grown a lot this year.

choices.text: A recruiter reached out with a much better offer, so I think we need to talk about my salary.
choices.reaction: Oh. Okay. Are you planning to leave?
choices.coachNote: Opening with another offer turns a raise talk into a retention scare. Now he's defending, not listening.
choices.betterLine: I want to talk about my pay. This year I took on Priya's work and shipped the billing migration.

trigger.label: You use another offer as a threat

partnerLine.guarded: Look, before we go further, is this about another offer? Because that changes things.
partnerLine.neutral: Okay. Walk me through it. What's changed in your role?
partnerLine.open: Yeah, the migration was a big deal. Walk me through the rest.

choices.text: When Priya left, I picked up the reporting pipeline on top of my work. The migration shipped two weeks early and cut failed payments by about 18%.
choices.reaction: Eighteen percent. I didn't know it was that high.
choices.coachNote: One concrete result with a number gives him something he can repeat to HR.

choices.text: Honestly, I've just been working really hard. Staying late, taking on whatever comes up.
choices.reaction: I know you work hard. Everyone here does, though.
choices.coachNote: Effort is real, but it's hard for him to argue for. Results travel further than hours.
choices.betterLine: I picked up the reporting pipeline, and the migration cut failed payments by about 18%.

choices.text: I mean, you've seen my work. I shouldn't have to spell it out.
choices.reaction: I'd actually like you to. That's what I'll have to do for HR.
choices.coachNote: It sounds confident, but it hands him the job of building your case.
choices.betterLine: Sure. The migration shipped two weeks early and cut failed payments by about 18%.

partnerLine.guarded: Alright. Even if I agree, the review cycle's in March. I can't do much before that.
partnerLine.neutral: Okay, that's solid. What are you asking for, exactly?
partnerLine.open: That's a strong year. So what number did you have in mind?

choices.text: I'm asking for a 15% raise. That brings me in line with what this role pays elsewhere, and I've got the data if it helps.
choices.reaction: Fifteen. Okay. That's specific. I appreciate that.
choices.coachNote: A clear number with a reason behind it is easy for him to take upstairs.

choices.text: Whatever you think is fair, honestly. I trust you.
choices.reaction: That's kind, but it doesn't really help me make the case.
choices.coachNote: Leaving the number to him feels generous, but he'll anchor low to stay safe on budget.
choices.betterLine: I'm asking for 15%. That's in line with what this role pays elsewhere.

choices.text: Sorry, I know budgets are tight. Maybe something small, if that's even possible?
choices.reaction: Something small. Okay. I'll see what I can do.
choices.coachNote: You negotiated against yourself before he said a word.
choices.betterLine: I'm asking for 15%, and I've got the market data if it helps.

partnerLine.guarded: I hear you. I'm just not sure I can promise anything right now.
partnerLine.neutral: I can't approve it myself, but I can take it to HR. Timing's the hard part.
partnerLine.open: I think I can make a case for this. Timing's the only tricky bit.

choices.text: That's fair. What would you need from me to make the case, and could we aim for a decision before March?
choices.reaction: Send me a one-pager with those numbers by Friday. I'll push for February.
choices.coachNote: You gave a little on timing, kept the ask, and left with a task and a date.

choices.text: Okay, no worries. Just let me know whenever you hear something.
choices.coachNote: Friendly, but "whenever" hands the timeline to a busy person. It may quietly drift.
choices.betterLine: What would you need from me to make the case, and by when?

choices.text: If it can't happen before March, I might need to look at other options.
choices.reaction: Then I guess you'll have to do what's right for you.
choices.coachNote: An ultimatum at the end undoes the case you built and puts him on the defensive.
choices.betterLine: That's fair. What do you need from me, and could we aim for before March?

trigger.label: You use another offer as a threat

endings.guarded: Let me think about it. I'll get back to you.
endings.neutral: Send me what you've got. I'll raise it with HR and let you know.
endings.open: Good conversation. Get me that one-pager and I'll fight for February.
